---
title: "Roadmap"
---

Every planned concept page, grouped into modules that follow a learning path. Falconer & Mackay (F&M, 4th ed.) supplies the theory and Fehr the applied methods; where both books cover a topic they share one page. Linked items are live.


## Module 1: Populations and gene frequency

*F&M ch. 1–2*

- [x] 1.1 [Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium](quantgen/hardy-weinberg.qmd)
- [ ] 1.2 Migration: Two populations converging with migration rate *m*
- [ ] 1.3 Mutation and mutation equilibrium: *p* over generations for forward/back mutation rates
- [x] 1.4 [Selection at a single locus](quantgen/selection-single-locus.qmd)
- [ ] 1.5 Mutation–selection balance: Equilibrium *q* vs *s* and *u*

## Module 2: Small populations, drift and inbreeding

*F&M ch. 3–5; Fehr, genotype frequencies under inbreeding*

- [x] 2.1 [Genetic drift](quantgen/genetic-drift.qmd)
- [ ] 2.2 Effective population size: *N*e from sex ratio, fluctuating size, family-size variance
- [ ] 2.3 Inbreeding coefficient and coancestry: Clickable pedigree; path-counting computes *F*
- [ ] 2.4 Regular systems of inbreeding: Heterozygosity decline under selfing, full-sib, half-sib, backcrossing
- [x] 2.5 [Homozygosity under selfing (Fehr)](cultivar/selfing-homozygosity.qmd)
- [ ] 2.6 Population size to recover a genotype (Fehr): Required *n* for a target probability, *k* loci, F₂ vs BC vs F∞

## Module 3: Genetic values and variance

*F&M ch. 6–8*

- [x] 3.1 [Continuous variation from many loci](quantgen/continuous-variation.qmd)
- [x] 3.2 [Genotypic values, *a* and *d*](quantgen/genotypic-values.qmd)
- [x] 3.3 [Average effect and breeding value](quantgen/genotypic-values.qmd)
- [x] 3.4 [Partitioning genetic variance](quantgen/variance-components.qmd)
- [ ] 3.5 Epistasis: Two-locus value table; how interaction variance appears
- [ ] 3.6 Environmental variance and G×E: Reaction norms; crossover vs scale interaction

## Module 4: Resemblance between relatives and heritability

*F&M ch. 9–10; Fehr, heritability*

- [ ] 4.1 Covariance between relatives: Table of covariances (P–O, HS, FS, sibs of inbreds) built from *V*A, *V*D
- [ ] 4.2 Parent–offspring regression: Simulated families; slope = ½*h*² or *h*²
- [ ] 4.3 Sib analysis and variance components: ANOVA of simulated half-sib/full-sib families; estimate *h*² and its SE
- [x] 4.4 [Heritability on a plot vs entry-mean basis (Fehr)](cultivar/heritability-entry-mean.qmd)
- [ ] 4.5 Precision of heritability estimates: SE of *h*² vs number of families and family size

## Module 5: Selection

*F&M ch. 11–13, 19; Fehr, selection and expected gain*

- [x] 5.1 [Heritability and response to selection](quantgen/heritability-selection.qmd)
- [x] 5.2 [Selection intensity](quantgen/selection-intensity.qmd)
- [ ] 5.3 Response over generations and limits: Multi-generation simulation with finite loci; plateau and allele fixation
- [x] 5.4 [Expected gain per cycle and per year (Fehr)](cultivar/expected-gain.qmd)
- [ ] 5.5 Family, within-family and combined selection: Accuracy vs intraclass correlation and family size
- [ ] 5.6 Correlated response and genetic correlation: Two-trait scatter; indirect vs direct selection
- [ ] 5.7 Selection index: Index weights for two traits; response in each trait
- [ ] 5.8 Independent culling and tandem selection: Compare with index at equal intensity

## Module 6: Inbreeding, crossbreeding and hybrids

*F&M ch. 14–16; Fehr, hybrid and synthetic cultivars*

- [x] 6.1 [Inbreeding depression](quantgen/inbreeding-depression.qmd)
- [ ] 6.2 Heterosis: F₁ and F₂ heterosis from allele-frequency differences and *d*
- [ ] 6.3 Redistribution of variance under inbreeding: Among-line vs within-line variance vs *F* (2*F*·VA vs (1−F)·VA)
- [ ] 6.4 General and specific combining ability: Diallel table; GCA/SCA from cross means
- [ ] 6.5 Synthetic cultivars: Syn₂ prediction from parents and F₁ means (Wright's formula); effect of number of parents
- [ ] 6.6 Hybrid cultivar development: Single, three-way, double cross; performance prediction

## Module 7: Scale, thresholds and QTL

*F&M ch. 17, 18, 21*

- [ ] 7.1 Scale and transformations: Log/sqrt transform removes interaction and skew
- [ ] 7.2 Threshold characters: Liability distribution, threshold, incidence; heritability on the liability scale
- [ ] 7.3 QTL detection: single-marker analysis: Marker–QTL distance vs detected effect
- [ ] 7.4 Interval mapping: LOD profile along a chromosome from simulated F₂ / RIL data
- [ ] 7.5 Marker-assisted selection: Gain from MAS vs phenotypic selection by *h*² and % variance explained

## Module 8: Breeding methods for self-pollinated crops

*Fehr*

- [ ] 8.1 Mass selection and pure-line selection: Selection among lines vs within a mixture
- [ ] 8.2 Pedigree method: Family tree from F₂ to F₆ with selection at each step
- [ ] 8.3 Bulk method: Natural selection drift in a bulk; frequency shifts
- [x] 8.4 [Single-seed descent vs bulk vs pedigree](cultivar/ssd-bulk-pedigree.qmd)
- [x] 8.5 [Backcrossing](cultivar/backcrossing.qmd)
- [ ] 8.6 Doubled haploids: DH vs SSD: time to homozygosity, variance among lines
- [ ] 8.7 Multiline cultivars: Component lines and disease resistance mixtures

## Module 9: Population improvement and cross-pollinated crops

*Fehr; F&M ch. 16*

- [x] 9.1 [Recurrent selection schemes](cultivar/recurrent-selection.qmd)
- [ ] 9.2 Reciprocal recurrent selection: Gain in cross performance between two populations
- [ ] 9.3 Clonal cultivars: Selection among clones; heterozygosity fixed
- [ ] 9.4 Mutation breeding: Mutation rate and population size needed to find a mutant

## Module 10: Field testing and cultivar evaluation

*Fehr*

- [ ] 10.1 Field plot technique: Plot size, border effects and CV
- [ ] 10.2 Spatial variation and blocking: Simulated field with a gradient; RCBD vs CRD precision
- [x] 10.3 [Allocating reps, locations and years](cultivar/resource-allocation.qmd)
- [ ] 10.4 Probability of correct selection: Chance the truly best line is selected vs *h*² and number of entries
- [ ] 10.5 Cultivar stability: Finlay–Wilkinson / Eberhart–Russell regression on environment index
- [ ] 10.6 Cultivar release and seed purity: Generations of seed increase; off-type frequency
